newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crude rallies hit Japan refiners -- industry head.
newsitem.headline: Crude rallies hit Japan refiners -- industry head.

text.p: Japanese refiners' profits have been squeezed severely due to higher crude oil prices as well as sluggish retail oil product prices, the head of Japan's oil industry body told a news conference on Wednesday.
"It's not pretty bad, it's really bad," said Yuji Idemitsu, president of the Petroleum Association of Japan.
The group comprises 24 major refiners and wholesalers.

Current profits of 12 leading oil firms fell 54 percent in the April-September period, compared with the previous half-year, a survey by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry showed earlier this week.
Idemitsu attributed the dwindling profit margins partly to firmer global crude oil prices.
Most oil firms in Japan adjust their wholesale prices based on fluctuations in crude prices and yen/dollar exchange rates.
As changes in crude oil prices are passed on to domestic wholesale prices two months later, refiners' profits come under pressure whenever crude prices are on the rise.
Despite higher crude oil prices, retail gasoline prices are sliding amid intense competition among service stations.
"What we are experiencing now is a highly unusual combination," said Idemitsu, who is also president of leading refiner Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd.

According to the government's Agency of Natural Resources and Energy, retail gasoline prices this week fell by one yen per litre from levels a week ago to 105 yen. A year ago, gasoline prices averaged 112 yen per litre at the pump.
Oil firms' profits have also been squeezed because some truck and bus firms, major customers of gas oil, have not accepted price hikes in gas oil, which most oil firms implemented last spring.

Following the deregulation of oil product imports in April, refiners introduced a new price system, which, in effect, lowered gasoline prices to the international level while raising kerosene and gas oil prices.
